examples.en: I grill tofu and dip it in soy sauce.
Please add just a little soy sauce.

examples.ko: 먹어 보고 싱거우면 간장을 더 넣어요.
examples.en: Taste it, and if it's bland, add more soy sauce.

examples.ko: 할머니 집에는 간장, 된장, 고추장이 있어요.
examples.en: At my grandmother's house, there are soy sauce, soybean paste and red pepper paste.
I put soy sauce and sesame oil in my egg rice.

examples.ko: 이 간장은 너무 짜서 조금만 써야 해요.
examples.en: This soy sauce is so salty that I should use only a little.

explain: 맛을 말할 때 '짜다', '싱겁다'와 자주 같이 나와요. 간장에는 진간장, 국간장처럼 종류가 있어서 요리에 따라 골라 써요.
explain_en: It often appears with taste words like '짜다' (salty) and '싱겁다' (bland). There are types such as 진간장 and 국간장, and cooks choose by dish.

examples.en: I bought napa cabbage at the market.

examples.ko: 김장 때문에 배추를 스무 포기 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought twenty heads of napa cabbage for making kimchi.
I tried making kimchi from napa cabbage in winter.
I put napa cabbage in and make doenjang soup.
Napa cabbage has green outer leaves and a yellow inside.

explain: “양배추”는 배추가 아니에요. 둥글고 단단한 서양식 양배추예요. 한국 김치에는 보통 배추를 써요.
explain_en: 양배추 is not 배추. It is the round, firm Western cabbage. Kimchi is usually made with 배추.

en: to pass on, to convey (news, a message, regards)

examples.ko: 제 동료가 우리 팀에 회의 소식을 전했어요.
examples.en: My coworker passed the meeting news on to our team.

examples.ko: 팀장님께 제가 좀 늦는다고 전해 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell the team leader I'll be a little late.
I told my friend that it will rain tomorrow.
I'll pass the company news on to you by email.

examples.ko: 이 편지를 동생에게 전해 줄 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can you hand this letter over to my younger sibling?

explain: 전하다는 다른 사람의 말, 소식, 마음을 대신 가져다준다는 느낌이에요. 내 생각을 직접 말할 때는 “말하다”를 써요.

dict_examples.en: To pass the happy news on to the family.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그는 형에게 어머니의 당부의 말씀을 전했다.
dict_examples.en: He conveyed his mother's words of request to his older brother.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 가끔 그를 찾아와 집안 소식을 전하던 고모가 안 나타난 지도 오래되었다.
dict_examples.en: It has been a long time since his aunt, who used to visit him and bring news of the family, last showed up.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 전하다 has the feel of carrying someone's words, news or feelings over to another person. When you just say your own thought, use 말하다.

examples.en: My dream is to be a businessperson.
My uncle is a businessman who runs a small company.

examples.ko: 그 사업가는 작은 가게에서 시작해서 큰 회사를 만들었어요.
examples.en: That businessman started in a small shop and built a big company.
My friend is famous as a young entrepreneur.
You need courage to become a businessperson.

explain: ‘사장’은 회사에서 가장 높은 자리고, ‘사업가’는 사업을 하는 사람이에요. 작은 가게 주인을 ‘사장님’이라고 부르지만, 보통 ‘사업가’라고 하지는 않아요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 아버지는 망해 가는 기업을 인수해서 다시 일으킨, 유능한 사업가이시다.
dict_examples.en: My father is a capable businessman who took over a failing company and revived it.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 사장 is the top position in a company; 사업가 is a person who does business. A small shop owner is called 사장님, but usually not 사업가.

examples.en: After work I had a glass of soju with a friend.
How about a glass of soju after so long?
I introduced soju to my foreign friend.

examples.ko: 한국 식당에서 소주는 보통 작은 잔에 따라 마셔요.
examples.en: In Korean restaurants, soju is usually poured into small glasses.
The soju glass is small, so it empties quickly.

examples.ko: 삼겹살을 먹을 때 소주 생각이 난다고 아버지가 말했어요.
examples.en: My father said he thinks of soju when he eats pork belly.

explain: 한국을 대표하는 술 중 하나로 보통 '한 잔', '한 병'으로 세요. 맥주와 섞은 것은 '소맥'이라고 해요. 어른과 함께 마실 때는 술을 두 손으로 받는 예절이 있어요.
explain_en: It is one of Korea's best-known drinks and is counted as '한 잔' (a glass) or '한 병' (a bottle). Soju mixed with beer is called '소맥'. When drinking with elders, there is an etiquette of receiving the drink with both hands.

examples.en: I add a little vinegar to cold noodles.
I wipe the window with vinegar.
I bought a bottle of vinegar.
The vinegar is too sour.
I sprinkle olive oil and vinegar on the salad.
The vinegar smell was strong, so I opened the window.

explain: 맛은 '시다'로 말해요. 줄여서 '초'라고도 하고 '초고추장'은 고추장에 식초를 넣은 소스예요. 요리뿐 아니라 청소에도 쓰는 사람이 많아요.
explain_en: Its taste is described with '시다' (sour). It is sometimes shortened to '초', and '초고추장' is red pepper paste mixed with vinegar. Many people use it for cleaning as well as cooking.

examples.en: I bought 20 kilograms of rice.
I wash the rice to cook it.
We've run out of rice, so I have to go to the supermarket.
The price of rice went up a lot this year.
I make rice cakes from rice.
This rice is delicious.

explain: 익히기 전은 '쌀', 익힌 것은 '밥', 논에서 자라는 식물은 '벼'예요. 쌀은 '씻다', '떨어지다'와 자주 같이 써요.
explain_en: Before cooking it is '쌀', cooked it is '밥', and the plant growing in the paddy is '벼'. '쌀' often goes with '씻다' (wash) and '떨어지다' (run out).

examples.en: The leaves in the park are turning red little by little.
My face goes red when I present in front of people.
After I ate spicy tteokbokki, my lips turned red.

examples.ko: 햇빛 아래 오래 있었더니 팔이 빨개졌어요.
examples.en: After being in the sun for a long time, my arms turned red.
When I'm embarrassed, even my ears turn red.

dict_examples.en: One's face turns red after a single drink.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 빨갛다 drops its ㅎ: 빨개요, 빨개지다. You don't say 빨갛아지다.
